about: Airspan Networks is a US wireless network equipment company, based in Boca Raton, Florida (the input lists Plano, Texas), supplying 4G and 5G radio access, small cells, fixed wireless and open RAN products to mobile operators and private network users. It went public via a SPAC in 2021 (NYSE American: MIMO) and filed for Chapter 11 in 2024. B2B network equipment supplier with no consumer brand awareness.
cb_desc: Airspan Networks provides 4G broadband wireless systems...

about: Columbus McKinnon designs and makes material handling equipment, such as hoists, cranes, chain, rigging and lifting products and intelligent motion control, serving industrial, entertainment, infrastructure and construction customers. Revenue near 1 billion dollars. Headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, with historic roots in Amherst, New York; founded 1875. Listed on Nasdaq (CMCO). B2B industrial brand with no consumer visibility, though its hoists are used in stage rigging.

Ceconomy is the German parent of consumer electronics retailers MediaMarkt and Saturn, which run hundreds of stores in Europe, with an online and services business. Revenue near 23 billion euros. Headquartered in Dusseldorf; separated from Metro in 2017. Listed in Frankfurt (CEC). China's JD.com agreed in 2025 to acquire Ceconomy for roughly 2.2 billion euros. MediaMarkt and Saturn are well-known consumer brands across Europe with a history of football and sports sponsorship.

wiki.title: Ceconomy
wiki.text: Ceconomy AG is an international retail company headquartered in Düsseldorf, Germany. Its history goes back to the Metro Group. Ceconomy operates more than 1,000 consumer electronics stores in eleven countries. In addition to MediaMarkt and Saturn, the group owns Deutsche Technikberatung. Approximately 24 % of its sales are generated online.

about: Micron Technology is a Boise, Idaho semiconductor maker, one of the three largest producers of DRAM memory and a major NAND flash maker. It sells memory and storage chips to data centers, AI server makers, smartphone, PC, automotive and industrial customers, and sells consumer SSDs and memory under the Crucial brand. Revenue is $25bn+ with around 48,000 employees and fabs in the US, Japan, Taiwan, Singapore and elsewhere. Listed on the Nasdaq (MU). Mostly a B2B brand, with Crucial giving some consumer and gamer awareness.

wiki.title: Micron Technology
wiki.text: Micron Technology, Inc. is an American multinational semiconductor company that manufactures computer memory and computer data storage products, including dynamic random-access memory (DRAM), flash memory, High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), and solid-state drives (SSDs). Founded in 1978 in Boise, Idaho, Micron is the only major American computer memory manufacturer. It is one of the "Big Three" computer memory manufacturers, along with the South Korean companies Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.

about: Forward Industries is a design, sourcing and manufacturing company for carry cases and protective solutions, historically for medical devices (diabetic kits), tools and consumer electronics, under its Forward Industries Design Group. In 2025 it pivoted to a Solana digital asset treasury strategy, with a large private placement led by Galaxy Digital, Jump Crypto and Multicoin. Listed on Nasdaq (FORD), with the HQ shown as Austin, Texas. Small B2B supplier turned crypto treasury vehicle, with no consumer awareness.

Cloover is a Berlin-based energy-transition fintech providing embedded financial services and software for solar, storage and heat-pump installers. It offers financing, a sales platform and project management software, enabling installers to sell energy systems to households. Founded around 2021 and has raised about $1.4 billion mostly as debt facilities, with offices in Germany and elsewhere in Europe. B2B, with limited public brand awareness.

about: Trench Group is a Germany-based maker of high-voltage electrical equipment such as instrument transformers, bushings and air-core reactors for utilities and industry. It was carved out from Siemens Energy in 2024 and is owned by Triton, the private equity firm, with a significant investment of about 1.4 billion. Operates plants in Germany, Canada, the US, Brazil and elsewhere. B2B industrial supplier with no consumer brand awareness.
cb_desc: Trench Group provides high- voltage products and solution..

about: Tata Electronics is the electronics manufacturing arm of the Tata Group, based in India, making precision components and assembling products such as Apple iPhones (acquired Wistron and Pegatron's Indian operations), and building a semiconductor fab in Dholera and an OSAT plant in Assam. Customers are global electronics brands. A Tata Sons subsidiary with major investments of over 100 billion rupees reported. B2B manufacturing; the Tata name has very high awareness in India.

Haier is a Qingdao, China-based home appliance maker, founded in 1984 and now part of Haier Smart Home (Shanghai, Hong Kong, Frankfurt: 600690, 6690), owning Haier, GE Appliances, Fisher & Paykel, Casarte, Candy and AQUA. Revenue is above 280 billion yuan, with products sold in more than 160 countries. Customers are consumers and builders. Very high household brand awareness worldwide, with sports sponsorship.

wiki.title: Haier
wiki.what: Chinese consumer electronics and appliance company
wiki.text: Haier Group Corporation is a Chinese multinational home appliances and consumer electronics company headquartered in Qingdao, Shandong. Its Haier Smart Home Company affiliate, of which it owns 35%, designs, develops, manufactures and sells home appliances including refrigerators, air conditioners, washing machines, dryers, and microwave ovens under the brand names Haier, Casarte, Leader, GE Appliances, Fisher & Paykel, Aqua, Candy and Evo. Its Haier Electronics Group affiliate manufactures consumer electronics such as mobile phones, computers, and televisions. about: ESWIN Computing is a Beijing-based Chinese semiconductor company developing RISC-V processors, AI chips and related electronics for industrial, automotive and consumer markets, founded around 2020 with significant funding from state-linked investors. It aims to supply SoCs and compute platforms to Chinese device makers. Customers are electronics manufacturers. B2B chip designer with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Frore Systems is a San Jose semiconductor company that makes AirJet solid-state active cooling chips, a silent, thin cooling technology for laptops, tablets, phones and data centres that replaces fans. Founded 2018 by Seshu Madhavapeddy, it has raised funding from venture investors including Mayfield at a valuation reported near 1 billion dollars. Customers are device makers. Revenue is chip sales. B2B component brand with limited consumer visibility, though recognised in tech media.

Rebellions is a South Korean AI chip company based in Seoul that designs neural processing units and accelerators for data centre AI inference, including ATOM and REBEL chips, and merged with Sapeon in 2024. It has raised funding from investors including Samsung, SK Telecom and KT with a valuation of over 1 billion dollars and targets cloud and enterprise customers. Founded 2020. B2B semiconductor brand with little consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: WT Microelectronics is a Taiwanese electronic components distributor headquartered in Taipei and listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (3036), distributing semiconductors, memory and other chips for brands such as Samsung, Qualcomm, Analog Devices and others to electronics manufacturers across Asia. Revenue is in the hundreds of billions of Taiwan dollars. B2B distributor with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: WT Microelectronics Co., Ltd. provider focusing on the globa...

about: Cambridge Industries USA is the US-facing division of Cambridge Industries Group (CIG), a Shanghai-based manufacturer of optical networking, broadband and telecom equipment such as ONUs, routers, optical modules and 5G devices for carriers and cloud providers worldwide. Founded 2000s and later taken private. Customers are telecom operators and data centre operators. B2B hardware supplier with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Cambridge Industries USA is the division of Cambridge....

about: Nearfield Instruments develops and supplies metrology and inspection equipment for semiconductor manufacturing, using atomic force microscopy based tools to measure nanoscale structures on chips, notably its QUADRA platform. Customers are leading chipmakers and equipment partners. Spun out of TNO and TU Delft, it is based in Rotterdam, Netherlands. Crunchbase shows about $598 million in total funding, latest June 2026. Private. Deep B2B industrial brand with no consumer visibility.

Tokyo-based Japanese precision-instrument maker, founded 1932, producing positioning and surveying equipment, ophthalmic eye-care instruments and smart agriculture and construction systems for professional customers worldwide. It was taken private by KKR-led investors after delisting from the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Revenue is around JPY 200 billion. B2B brand with moderate visibility in optics and surveying. Topcon employs about 5,000 people and sells through distributors in more than 100 countries, and also makes ophthalmic equipment used by eye clinics.

Bright Machines is a San Francisco company offering microfactories that use software-defined robotics and AI for flexible electronics and high-tech manufacturing, selling to customers like Nvidia, Microsoft and other electronics makers. Founded in 2018, it has raised about 437 million dollars, with investors including Nvidia and Microsoft. Revenue comes from hardware, software and services. B2B industrial technology with low consumer awareness.

Polar Semiconductor is a US semiconductor foundry in Bloomington, Minnesota that manufactures power, sensor and automotive-grade chips on 200mm wafers for customers in automotive, industrial and aerospace markets. It earns money through contract wafer manufacturing. It was formerly owned by Sanken Electric and Allegro MicroSystems and was recapitalised in 2024 with a large US CHIPS Act award and private investment, with the Crunchbase total funding at about $298 million. B2B supplier with little consumer brand awareness.

Growatt New Energy is a Shenzhen-based Chinese manufacturer of solar inverters, residential energy storage systems, EV chargers and related monitoring software, founded in 2011. It sells through installers and distributors to homeowners and businesses in over 100 countries and is one of the largest residential inverter makers by shipments. Revenue is in the low billions of dollars. Crunchbase shows about CNY 1.08 billion of funding. The brand is well known to installers and in the solar trade, but consumer awareness is modest.

Spectris plc is a London based UK maker of precision measurement instruments and test equipment, through brands including Malvern Panalytical, HBK (Hottinger Bruel & Kjaer) and Omega, serving pharmaceutical, semiconductor, automotive and industrial customers. Spectris has had motorsport links through its HBK and Spectris partnerships with Formula 1 teams. It was listed on the London Stock Exchange (SXS) and was acquired by KKR in 2025 after a bidding contest with Advent, for about 4.2 billion pounds.

Pragmatic Semiconductor is a UK company in Cambridge that makes ultra-low-cost flexible integrated circuits on thin plastic-like substrates, using thin-film transistor technology rather than silicon. These chips target packaging, healthcare, wearables and IoT items where cost matters. Founded in 2010 as a spin-out of Cambridge University and Plastic Logic, with its fab at Sedgefield, County Durham, it has raised around 400 million dollars from Cambridge Innovation Capital and UK government sources. B2B component maker with no consumer brand.

Figment is a Toronto-based provider of institutional-grade staking and blockchain infrastructure, running validator nodes and wallet APIs for proof-of-stake networks such as Ethereum, Solana and Cosmos for exchanges, funds and wallets. Revenue comes from a share of staking rewards and fees. Founded in 2018, it has raised about $164 million, including a Series C. B2B crypto infrastructure with limited mainstream consumer awareness.

Connecteam is a New York-based, Israeli-founded multi-functional workforce management app for frontline and deskless employees, combining scheduling, time tracking, task management, internal communication and training, sold by monthly subscription. Founded in 2014, it raised a $120 million round in 2024 from Spectrum Equity, bringing funding to about $158 million. Customers are small and medium businesses across industries. B2B software with limited consumer awareness.

SmartSens Technology is a Shanghai-based Chinese fabless designer of high-performance CMOS image sensors used in security cameras, smartphones, cars and machine vision. Customers are consumer electronics, camera and automotive manufacturers. Founded in 2011, it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2022. Crunchbase shows about $244 million raised before listing. B2B semiconductor brand with little consumer awareness, though its sensors sit inside many products.

AirTrunk is an Australian hyperscale data center operator, founded in 2014 by Robin Khuda and based in Sydney, with campuses across Australia, Singapore, Hong Kong, Japan, Malaysia and Indonesia, serving cloud and AI customers such as Microsoft, Google and Alibaba. It was acquired in 2024 by Blackstone and CPP Investments for about A$24bn. Revenue is earned from long-term data center capacity contracts. Private. B2B infrastructure with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: AirTrunk
wiki.text: AirTrunk is an Australian data centre company founded by Robin Khuda in 2015, and sold to Blackstone for A$24 billion. The company operates more than 3 GW of operating and planned capacity across 20 sites in six countries: Australia, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, Hong Kong, and India.

about: EdgeConneX is a Herndon, Virginia data center developer and operator that builds edge and hyperscale facilities in North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific for cloud providers, content companies and enterprises. It has been owned by EQT Infrastructure since 2018, which took over from Providence Equity. Private, with funding mainly debt. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.
